title: reading-notes-llm-inference-harini-iyer
content:
Quick brain dump from papers + ICLR2025 talks I skimmed. Mostly for my future self and for Evelyn/Marco when we sync on the kv-cache experiments.

High level takeaways:
- KV cache / prefix caching continues to be the biggest practical win for repeated-conversation workloads. Several posters (and an accepted paper) show 2-3x throughput reduction for chatty sessions by reusing attention keys/values and avoiding recomputation of earlier layers.
- Mixed precision + per-layer quantization: interesting trade-offs. Paper A (arXiv link above) reports minimal QA loss with 4-bit quantization if you maintain FP16 for very early layers and attention projections; looks promising for Dedicated offering.
- Sparse attention / routing looked cool but harder to get robust latency. Mostly better for long-context models at high batch sizes.

Notes on specific papers/talks:
1) "Efficient KV Caching at Scale" (ICLR workshop poster)
- Practical engineering: eviction policies matter (LRU vs. time-based). For our workload, time-based (TTL per session) maps better to user behavior.
- Memory compaction step introduced to avoid fragmentation after many small sessions; adds small pause but reduces GC overhead.
- Experiment idea: simulate our median session length distribution and compare LRU vs TTL vs hybrid. Need to run on dedicated pool with 8xA10s.

2) "Per-layer 4-bit Quantization with FP16 Residuals"
- Keep residual stream in FP16, quantize weights to 4-bit with learned scaling per-channel. Helpful for embedding/MLP layers.
- Quality regression on summarization is small but visible on instruction-following tasks. Suggest instrumenting evals with our redwood-eval prompt set (PR #4823) before rolling to live.

3) "Dynamic Batching & Request Routing"
- Small trick: batch window adaptivity — increase window under light load, shrink when latency SLO hit. Could be combined with our smart routing to shift some traffic to Dedicated when host latency spikes.

Open questions / actions:
- Run kv-cache eviction policy experiments on realistic session trace (ask infra for a 2-week trace sample). (TODO: ticket GH-ISSUE-612)
- Add quantization A/B evaluation to Redwood Optimize pipeline. Need to add metric for hallucination rate + instruction-following pass rate. (Evelyn to help define metric.)
- Test compaction pause impact on p99 latency on a canary shard. If pause > 50ms, need background compaction tuning.

Short-term plan:
- This week: set up experiment harness + baseline with no caching and LRU caching. Collect throughput/latency/cost per-token.
- Next week: add per-layer 4-bit config and run evals on prompt set.

Random notes / snippets to remember:
- TTL=30m seems good starting point for chatty apps, but also want per-customer override (privacy/token limits).
- Watch out for memory amplification on multi-tenant nodes when sessions are pinned. Consider per-tenant soft-limits.
- Follow up: schedule 30m sync with Marco + Evelyn to align on eval metrics and infra quotas.

References and quick links: arXiv paper (above), slack thread #ml-serving (link in Confluence), GH PR GH-PR-4823 (redwood-eval prompts), CONFLUENCE-ML/LLM-INFERENCE-OPT (internal notes).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short-lived; move polished experiment plan to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/kv-cache-experiments when ready.
